# Ranking invariance, calibration, and full-set recovery are distinct promises

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/system-one/candidate-invariance.md) · English

Updated 2026-10-27 · 3 topic entries / 3 representative comparisons

Prism-1 constrains scoring dependencies, the JEV request audit designs paired interventions, and the multiple-correct audit checks whether a distribution recovers the correct set. They answer different questions: what the architecture guarantees, what the experiment changes, and what the evaluation measures. A valid output or one top-1 score cannot stand in for these answers.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Freeze the evidence before discussing independence

Prism-1 assumes that shared state and the question are unchanged. An eligibility-only request audit keeps all displayed evidence fixed. If a new passage clarifies the question, score changes may reflect a reasonable information update. Compare A-versus-B conditional probabilities or odds. A drop in absolute probability caused by a larger softmax denominator is not a preference reversal.

Sources: [Prism-1: Position- and Rival-Independent Scoring for System One Models](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22066-prism-1/README-en.md) · [The Company a Question Keeps: Auditing Open Jev-Style Models for Retrieval](../../../../system-one/2610.14631-request-audit/README-en.md)

### Independent scores do not automatically yield multilabel probabilities

Even when Prism-1 makes each score independent of other options, the option softmax distributes a single unit of mass. The multiple-correct audit asks whether the entire correct set can be recovered. Correct options still compete for mass, so stable rankings do not imply that all correct options clear one threshold or that option shares are calibrated per-option correctness probabilities.

Sources: [Prism-1: Position- and Rival-Independent Scoring for System One Models](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22066-prism-1/README-en.md) · [When Multiple Choices Are Correct: Asymmetric Probability Allocation in Jev and Other Decision Models](../../../../system-one/2610.29217-jev-multicorrect/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### If A's probability drops when an unrelated C is added, has the property Prism-1 protects already been violated? {#cross-denominator-not-reversal}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Not necessarily. Fix the evidence, then compare A-to-B odds or A/(A+B). C raises the denominator, so A's absolute share can drop normally. Only a change in the old pair's relative preference calls for investigating cross-option information or position dependence. The request audit separates this normalization effect from added evidence.

    **Illustrative example:** With exponentiated scores 2 and 1, A has 2/3 of the mass. Adding C with score 5 lowers A's share to 2/8, but A/B remains 2; the old candidates have not reversed.

    Sources: [Prism-1: Position- and Rival-Independent Scoring for System One Models](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22066-prism-1/README-en.md) · [The Company a Question Keeps: Auditing Open Jev-Style Models for Retrieval](../../../../system-one/2610.14631-request-audit/README-en.md)

### Why is ranking every correct option ahead of every incorrect option insufficient to solve a multiple-answer question? {#cross-ranking-versus-set-recovery}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** A ranking gives relative order, not how many options to select. Option softmax distributes one unit of mass, so the second correct option may have little mass. A fixed threshold may omit it, and lowering the threshold may admit an incorrect option. Measure exact-set recovery separately and select thresholds on independent validation data.

    **Illustrative example:** A and B are correct and the shares are 0.60, 0.25, and 0.15. The ranking is perfect, but a threshold of 0.4 returns only A. Correct top-1 does not expose the missing B.

    Sources: [When Multiple Choices Are Correct: Asymmetric Probability Allocation in Jev and Other Decision Models](../../../../system-one/2610.29217-jev-multicorrect/README-en.md) · [Prism-1: Position- and Rival-Independent Scoring for System One Models](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22066-prism-1/README-en.md)

### Why must adding C as an eligible candidate and adding evidence describing C be tested separately? {#cross-evidence-versus-eligibility}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Eligibility changes the action set; evidence changes what the model knows. Prism-1 constrains independent option scores under fixed shared evidence only. The request audit separates interventions to distinguish competition effects from legitimate information updates. Multiple-correct scores must also be interpreted under fixed input conditions and a fixed correct set.

    **Illustrative example:** If tool C is already described in full, making it selectable changes eligibility. Adding “C supports offline operations” introduces new evidence that can change the A/B preference.

    Sources: [The Company a Question Keeps: Auditing Open Jev-Style Models for Retrieval](../../../../system-one/2610.14631-request-audit/README-en.md) · [Prism-1: Position- and Rival-Independent Scoring for System One Models](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22066-prism-1/README-en.md)
